content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) classifies albuminuria into three distinct categories for the purpose of assessing and monitoring chronic kidney disease (CKD): 1. Category A1: This represents normal to mildly increased levels of albumin in the urine, defined as less than 30 milligrams of albumin per gram of creatinine (<30 mg/g). 2. Category A2: This indicates a moderately increased level of albumin in the urine, with values ranging between 30 and 299 milligrams of albumin per gram of creatinine (30–299 mg/g). 3. Category A3: This reflects a severely increased level of albumin in the urine, characterized by values equal to or greater than 300 milligrams of albumin per gram of creatinine (≥300 mg/g).
